content:
Each tile is a \(T\)-tetromino containing \(4\) unit squares.

1. The \(5\times 4\) rectangle contains \(20\) unit squares, so area alone gives an upper bound of
   \[
   \frac{20}{4}=5.
   \]

2. Color the rectangle like a checkerboard. It has \(10\) squares of each color. Every \(T\)-tile covers three squares of one color and one square of the other color.

   If five tiles covered the rectangle, and \(k\) of them covered three black squares, then the number of black squares covered would be
   \[
   3k+(5-k)=5+2k,
   \]
   which is odd. It therefore cannot equal the \(10\) black squares in the rectangle. Hence five tiles are impossible.

3. Four tiles can be placed as follows, where equal letters form one tile and dots are uncovered squares:
   \[
   \begin{array}{ccccc}
   \cdot&A&B&B&B\\
   A&A&A&B&D\\
   \cdot&C&D&D&D\\
   C&C&C&\cdot&D
   \end{array}
   \]
   Each of \(A,B,C,D\) is a \(T\)-shaped tile, and none overlap.

Therefore, the maximum number of tiles is
\[
\boxed{4}.
\]
